lines.en: Mia, I feel terrible. Your sister just told me you’ve been ill all week, and if I had known, I would have called earlier.
lines.pt: Mia, estou me sentindo péssima. Sua irmã acabou de me contar que você está doente a semana toda, e se eu soubesse, teria ligado antes.

lines.en: Don’t be silly, Lily. Nobody at work even noticed.
lines.pt: Não seja boba, Lily. Ninguém no trabalho nem percebeu.

lines.en: Still, you sound exhausted. Have you seen a doctor, or are you planning to wait until it clears up by itself?
lines.pt: Mesmo assim, você parece exausta. Foi ao médico, ou está planejando esperar até passar sozinha?

lines.en: I went yesterday. She said I’d probably picked up a virus at the office, where half the team has been sneezing for days.
lines.pt: Fui ontem. Ela disse que eu provavelmente peguei um vírus no escritório, onde metade da equipe espirra há dias.

lines.en: That doesn’t surprise me. I wish I had come sooner, though.
lines.pt: Isso não me surpreende. Mas queria ter vindo antes.

lines.en: Actually, the neighbors have been wonderful. One of them brought soup, and another offered to pick up my prescription. Without them, this week would be so much lonelier.
lines.pt: Na verdade, os vizinhos têm sido maravilhosos. Um trouxe sopa, e outro se ofereceu para buscar a minha receita. Sem eles, esta semana seria muito mais solitária.

lines.en: That’s reassuring. Did the doctor say how long it’ll take to recover?
lines.pt: Que bom saber. A médica disse quanto tempo leva para se recuperar?

lines.en: She told me to rest for at least a week. If I hadn’t gone out in the rain on Monday, I wouldn’t have caught a second cold, but I couldn’t resist the walk.
lines.pt: Ela me mandou descansar pelo menos uma semana. Se eu não tivesse saído na chuva na segunda, não teria pegado um segundo resfriado, mas não resisti ao passeio.

lines.en: Typical you! Well, I’m staying tonight. I’ll make dinner, and you can tell me all about that book you’ve been reading since you’re stuck in bed.
lines.pt: Típico de você! Bem, vou ficar hoje à noite. Preparo o jantar, e você me conta tudo sobre aquele livro que anda lendo, já que está presa na cama.

lines.en: Oh, it’s gloomy, set on the moors, and full of storms and broken hearts. Honestly, it makes my cough seem cheerful by comparison.
lines.pt: Ah, é sombrio, passado nos pântanos, cheio de tempestades e corações partidos. Sinceramente, perto dele a minha tosse parece animada.

lines.en: Ha! Then I’ll bring something lighter next time, plus honey and lemon for that throat. Now get comfortable and tell me where it all begins.
lines.pt: Ha! Então da próxima vez trago algo mais leve, além de mel e limão para essa garganta. Agora fique à vontade e me conte por onde tudo começa.

facts.big: If + had + particípio, would have + particípio
facts.label: 3º condicional
facts.sub: Se eu soubesse, teria ligado: If I had known, I would have called. Se não tivesse ido…: If I hadn’t gone, I wouldn’t have… Arrependimento: I wish I had…

facts.label: Se eu tivesse
facts.sub: A primeira parte do 3º condicional usa if + had + particípio: If I had known you were ill… Em português, “se eu soubesse” ou “se eu tivesse sabido”. Nunca use would depois de if: If I would have known é erro.

facts.label: Teria
facts.sub: A segunda parte usa would have + particípio: …I would have called earlier. Em português, “teria ligado”. Na fala, vira I’d have called. Para negar, use wouldn’t have + particípio.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “If I had known” talks about a past that did not happen.
We say “If I would have known.”
items.why: We say If I had known.

items.s: “I would have called” is the result part.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: “If I had known” talks about a past that did not happen. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “If I would have known.” → Falso (We say If I had known.)
“I would have called” is the result part. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A visit to a sick friend · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey Sunday afternoon in a quiet street in Leeds. Eli rings the bell of a small terraced house. His friend Ana opens the door in a warm jumper. She has been ill for almost a week. Eli had no idea about it until this morning. Now both of them think about what could have been different.

“Ana, I feel terrible. If I had known you were ill, I would have called earlier.” says Eli. “Don’t worry, Eli. If I had told you, you would have worried too much.” says Ana. “True. But if I hadn’t been so busy, I would have noticed your cough last week.” says Eli.

paragraphs: “Well, if you hadn’t been so kind, I would have felt much lonelier this week.” says Ana. “I wish I had come sooner. Next time, I will call before I drive over.” says Eli. Eli puts the soup on the kitchen table. Ana laughs for the first time in days. They watch an old film on the sofa. Rain taps softly against the window. Eli promises to call every week from now on. Sometimes a friend is the best medicine.
